findings.pdf_says: In the 13.18.60.2 USAGE clause general format, the four brace groups 'BINARY-CHAR { SIGNED / UNSIGNED }', 'BINARY-SHORT { SIGNED / UNSIGNED }', 'BINARY-LONG { SIGNED / UNSIGNED }' and 'BINARY-DOUBLE { SIGNED / UNSIGNED }' print SIGNED WITHOUT an underline and UNSIGNED WITH an underline. Verified on the 300 dpi render of page 533 and again on a 5x tight crop of the BINARY-CHAR brace (E:/Temp/specrecon/f4/crop_533_900_620.png): no rule under 'SIGNED', a full-width rule under 'UNSIGNED'. The same asymmetry repeats in all four rows.
findings.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md, page-533 figure notes: "> **Figure notes (USAGE clause general format).** Underlined in the printed standard (required words / required minimum abbreviation): `USAGE`, `BINARY`, `BINARY-CHAR`, `BINARY-SHORT`, `BINARY-LONG`, `BINARY-DOUBLE`, `SIGNED`, `UNSIGNED`, `BIT`, ... `IS`, `OF`, `TO`, and `WITH` are not underlined." — SIGNED is listed among the underlined (required) words.
findings.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6.2/5.2.6.3, an underlined uppercase word is a REQUIRED word and a non-underlined uppercase word is an OPTIONAL word that may be omitted without changing the meaning. Because SIGNED is printed unmarked, the brace group '{ SIGNED / UNSIGNED }' is satisfiable by writing nothing at all, so USAGE BINARY-CHAR, USAGE BINARY-CHAR SIGNED and USAGE BINARY-CHAR UNSIGNED are all legal (likewise -SHORT, -LONG, -DOUBLE). Promoting SIGNED to a required word makes the brace a mandatory two-way choice, which rejects the bare 'USAGE BINARY-CHAR' / 'USAGE BINARY-LONG' spellings that real COBOL source uses constantly. This is the same falsely-restrictive direction of loss the sweep is hunting: legal source made to look illegal. A compiler or a reviewer working from this note would emit a diagnostic for conforming source, and would mis-classify SIGNED as a reserved required word rather than an optional word.
findings.suggested_repair: In the page-533 figure note, remove `SIGNED` from the underlined list and add it to the not-underlined list ("`IS`, `OF`, `TO`, `WITH`, and `SIGNED` are not underlined"), then state explicitly that because SIGNED is an optional word the four BINARY-* brace groups admit three spellings each: `BINARY-CHAR`, `BINARY-CHAR SIGNED`, and `BINARY-CHAR UNSIGNED` (and correspondingly for BINARY-SHORT, BINARY-LONG, BINARY-DOUBLE).
